sentences.text: We create two marker arrays.
Row 0 has one boolean for every row.
Col 0 has one boolean for every column.
Initially, everything is false.
Now scan the matrix.
Our first original 0 is at row 0, column 2.
So mark row 0, true, and column 2, true.
The next original 0 is at row 2, column 0.
So row 2, true, column 0, true.
Then we reach the interior 0 at row 3, column 3.
Mark row 3, true, column 3, true.
Discovery is finished.
Our row markers are true, false, true, true, false.
And our column markers are true, false, true, true, false.
Now the information flows back into the matrix.
Take row 1.
Its row marker is false, so row 1 is not completely 0.
But column 0 is marked, so the first cell becomes 0.
Column 1 is not marked, so 7 stays.
Column 2 is marked, so 8 becomes 0.
Column 3 is marked, so 9 becomes 0.
Column 4 is not marked, so 10 stays.
Now row 2, its row marker is true.
That one fact is enough.
Every cell in row 2 becomes 0.
The same happens to row 3.
Its row marker is also true.
Finally, row 4 is not marked.
So only the marked columns change.
22 survives.
23 becomes 0.
24 becomes 0.
25 survives.
And we reach the same correct answer.
This time, we did not preserve the whole matrix.
We preserved only the information that matters.
Now let's convert this idea into code.
